answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents stake tokens to form a sparse interaction graph. Clusters undergo game-theoretic multi-agent auditing where verifiers check topological cut verifications across clusters; if cut densities reveal fake identity partitions, stake slashing imposes superlinear attacker cost. In this design, honest agent clusters form an ocean of liquidity, while fraudulent subgraphs face ferrous enforcement and forfeit their opal stake reserves.
